content.description: Illustration showing measurement of piston diameter using a micrometer at 22mm from the piston pin center line, positioned at right angles to the piston pin center line

items: (a) Using a micrometer, measure the piston diameter at right angles to the piston pin center line, 22 mm (0.87 in.) from the piston pin.
(b) Check that the difference between the cylinder diameter and the piston diameter is within specification. (See step 5 on page EM-48)

content.text: If not within specification, replace the piston and/or rebore all six cylinders. (See page EM-52)

content.text: 3. MEASURE CLEARANCE BETWEEN PISTON RING GROOVE AND PISTON RING
Using a feeler gauge, measure the clearance between the piston ring and the ring land.
If the clearance is greater than maximum, replace the piston ring and if necessary, the piston

content.description: Illustration showing measurement of ring groove clearance using a feeler gauge inserted between piston ring and ring land

items: (a) Insert the piston ring into the cylinder bore.
(b) Using a piston, push the piston ring to beyond the bottom of the ring travel. (100 mm {3.94 in.} from top surface of cylinder block)
(c) Using a feeler gauge, measure the end gap.

content.text: If not within specification, replace the ring. Do not file the ring end.

content.description: Two diagrams showing ring end gap measurement. Left diagram shows cross-section of cylinder with piston and 100mm measurement from top. Right diagram shows top view of ring with feeler gauge measuring end gap

content.text: At 60°C (140°F), the pin should be able to be pushed into the piston with your thumb.
If the pin can be installed at a lower temperature, replace the piston and pin.
